name: devchar-passives-res
description: loop-filter series-resistor comparison -- 7 poly-resistor candidates, sheet resistance / head resistance / voltage coefficient
claim: #4 -> #10 (design-input, not a spec line) -- poly-resistor option for the loop-filter series resistor: sheet-resistance spread across `res_ff`/`res_ss` and temperature coefficient for `ppolyf_u` vs. the high-sheet variants.
methodology: Measurement topology: every device sits between a shared swept node and ground through its own 0 V ammeter, substrate grounded; a DC sweep of that node 0 -> 1.0 V in 25 mV steps gives R(V) = V/I, so the voltage coefficient is measured rather than assumed. Two drawn lengths per device (10 um and 50 um at W = 1 um; ppolyf_u additionally at W = 2 um) let rsh_eff = (R_50um - R_10um) / squares-between-lengths cancel the fixed contact head resistance; rhead is the remaining intercept (both terminals). rsh_eff differs from the model rsh parameter by the effective-width narrowing, which is why it is measured rather than quoted.
vcoef (%/V) is the fractional change in R of the 50 um device between 0.1 V and 1.0 V across it.

Corner axis: the res_* sections are an INDEPENDENT axis from the MOS tt/ff/ss/fs/sf sections used by devchar-delay / devchar-cp, and every device here depends only on that axis. `typical` is the harness bundle that carries res_typical; `res_ff` / `res_ss` skew the resistor family alone. The five MOS bundles are therefore not swept -- they would re-run the identical resistor-only circuit five times. Supply is likewise not an axis: the 0 -> 1.0 V device sweep IS this deck's voltage axis. Both omissions must be declared on the command line, e.g. `python3 sim/run_corners.py devchar-passives-res --subset-reason 'resistor-only DUT: res_* is the governing process axis; the device R-V sweep is the voltage axis, supply is not'`.

Temperature coefficient (tc_ppm_per_c = (R(125C) - R(-40C)) / (R(27C) * 165 C), from the body-dominated 50 um device) is NOT a per-point measurement -- it is a relation ACROSS the temperature axis. Read it off this record's per-corner r50 rows; the pre-migration runner precomputed it into res_tempco.csv, which record 20260731-041346-833292f still carries.
Solver: abstol=1e-15, reltol=1e-7 (the pre-migration deck's `.option` card, verbatim).
Statistical switches: sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0 (nominal skew, no Monte Carlo).
